target.title: fix(discord): sustained gateway bursts stop growing memory
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a connected Discord bot that produces regular Gateway commands faster than Discord's send window can retain an unlimited number of pending payloads. Sustained presence updates or member requests could therefore keep growing memory while increasingly stale events waited for later rate-limit windows.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Discord-owned Gateway send limiter now keeps at most one additional 120-event window. Once that backlog is full, another non-critical send fails synchronously instead of extending the queue. Heartbeats, voice-state updates, normal sends below the limit, timer-based draining, reconnect cleanup, and the 4 KiB payload guard are unchanged.

The caller contract is explicit at every reachable ordinary-send path. Auto-presence contains and logs send failures without marking the desired presence as applied, so its interval retries after the backlog or socket recovers. The manual `set-presence` action returns the rejection through the existing async action boundary. Ready-listener failures are already contained by the Discord event queue, and `requestGuildMembers()` currently has no production caller.

The 120-item bound follows Discord's documented contract of 120 Gateway events per connection every 60 seconds: https://docs.discord.com/developers/events/gateway#rate-limiting. Keeping more than one full window would retain extra memory only to replay older state after an additional minute or more.

## User Impact

Long-running Discord connections no longer accumulate an unbounded in-memory send backlog during sustained Gateway overload. Excess manual presence changes fail as an action error, automatic presence updates log and retry, and critical connection-maintenance events continue to bypass the ordinary queue.

## Evidence

The evidence below covers the pre-fix failure, a real loopback WebSocket run through the production Gateway implementation, each reachable ordinary-send caller, adjacent Gateway behavior, and repository checks. Terminal output is copied from the final local diff unless a section is explicitly labeled as the pre-fix red run.

### Current-main failure proof

Before the limiter change, the production `GatewayPlugin` loopback regression failed because the 241st regular event was silently appended instead of rejected:

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/internal/gateway-rate-limit.loopback.test.ts

RUN  v4.1.10

❯ |extension-discord| extensions/discord/src/internal/gateway-rate-limit.loopback.test.ts (1 test | 1 failed)
    × rejects sends after one full gateway window is queued

AssertionError: expected [Function] to throw an error

Test Files  1 failed (1)
Tests       1 failed (1)

[test] failed 1 Vitest shard
```

Before caller containment, the auto-presence regression also demonstrated that the new queue-full error escaped its timer-owned evaluation path:

```text
× contains gateway send failures and retries the same presence
expected [Function] to not throw
Received: Error: Discord gateway outbound queue is full

Test Files  1 failed (1)
Tests       1 failed | 5 passed (6)
```

The final pre-push `origin/main` was `4e11da2872eccadeaf4fbd9b7c8a6bf4b229adbe`. Its limiter still has an unbounded `outboundQueue.push(...)`, and its auto-presence path still calls `updatePresence()` without send-error containment.

### Real loopback WebSocket proof

The final regression uses the production `GatewayPlugin` over a real loopback WebSocket connection. It exhausts the live 120-event send window, fills one 120-event backlog, rejects one additional normal event, and proves that a critical heartbeat still crosses the same socket.

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/internal/gateway-rate-limit.loopback.test.ts --reporter=verbose

RUN  v4.1.10

stdout | extensions/discord/src/internal/gateway-rate-limit.loopback.test.ts > GatewayPlugin loopback rate limit > rejects sends after one full gateway window is queued
[discord gateway loopback proof] sent=121 queued=120 overflow=rejected critical=bypassed

✓ |extension-discord| extensions/discord/src/internal/gateway-rate-limit.loopback.test.ts > GatewayPlugin loopback rate limit > rejects sends after one full gateway window is queued 211ms

Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       1 passed (1)

[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 8.70s
```

### Caller-level overflow containment

The auto-presence test starts the production controller, injects its interval callback, makes the first Gateway update throw queue-full, then verifies the interval retries the same presence successfully. The manual action test verifies the same error becomes a rejected action Promise.

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/monitor/auto-presence.test.ts extensions/discord/src/actions/runtime.presence.test.ts

RUN  v4.1.10

Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests       25 passed (25)
Duration    19.77s

[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 28.40s
```

Production caller audit:

- `GatewayPlugin.updatePresence()` is reached by manual `set-presence`, auto-presence, and the READY status listener.
- Auto-presence now catches the synchronous failure, logs it, and leaves `lastAppliedSignature` / `lastAppliedAt` unchanged so the same desired value is retried.
- Manual `set-presence` is awaited through `handleDiscordPresenceAction()` -> `handleDiscordAction()` -> `handleDiscordMessageAction()`, so queue-full is returned through the existing action failure boundary.
- READY listeners execute through `DiscordEventQueue`; listener failures are logged and settled by `runJob()` instead of becoming unhandled process rejections. Reconnect paths also clear the queued payloads before the next READY.
- `requestGuildMembers()` has no production caller in the repository; its validation tests remain unchanged.

### Adjacent Gateway behavior

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/internal/gateway-rate-limit.loopback.test.ts extensions/discord/src/internal/gateway.test.ts

RUN  v4.1.10

Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests       28 passed (28)

[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 10.06s
```

### Formatting, lint, and repository guards

```text
$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check extensions/discord/src/monitor/auto-presence.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/auto-presence.test.ts extensions/discord/src/actions/runtime.presence.test.ts
All matched files use the correct format.

$ ./node_modules/.bin/oxlint extensions/discord/src/monitor/auto-presence.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/auto-presence.test.ts extensions/discord/src/actions/runtime.presence.test.ts
# passed with no diagnostics

$ git diff --check
# passed with no output
```

`node scripts/check-changed.mjs` selected `extensions` and `extensionTests`. The trusted-source local fallback passed conflict markers, max-lines ratchet, changelog attribution, extension export guards, duplicate coverage, dependency pins, formatting, Plugin SDK API baseline, deprecated API usage, plugin boundaries, package patches, and temp-creation checks. Extension typecheck then stopped on three unrelated errors in unchanged `packages/net-policy/src/ip.ts` (`benchmarking`, `orchid2`, and the IPv4/IPv6 union call). This PR does not touch that package. Exact-head PR CI remains the broad type/build gate.

Remote Testbox delegation was unavailable because this host has no `blacksmith` executable.

### Review and dependency contracts

- Official Discord contract: apps may send 120 Gateway events per connection per 60 seconds and are disconnected for exceeding it.
- Installed `ws@8.21.0` contract inspected: `WebSocket.send()` throws synchronously while CONNECTING; the Gateway already checks OPEN immediately before both enqueue and actual send.
- Sibling policy: Discord's REST scheduler and event queue already reject new work synchronously/explicitly when their configured queue bounds are reached.
- No config, environment variable, protocol, SDK, dependency, storage, or migration surface changes.

Fresh structured autoreview was attempted twice with the repository helper, Codex `gpt-5.6-sol`, and high reasoning. The first run included focused tests; the second disabled web search to isolate the failure. Both model runs ended after about 17 minutes with `codex engine failed (1)` and returned neither findings nor a clean verdict. A no-tools attempt did not invoke the engine because Codex autoreview does not support that option.

A manual review then covered the full limiter and Gateway modules, WebSocket callee, all ordinary and critical callers, READY event containment, sibling bounded queues, adjacent tests, current-main behavior, and the official Discord / installed `ws` contracts. No actionable in-scope finding remained. The autoreview infrastructure failure is not represented as a clean model verdict.
